title: Far Eastern Air Transport 103
summary: The Boeing 737 had lost cabin pressure twice: once on August 5 and again on takeoff August 22 before the flight was aborted. After repairs, the aircraft departed again and 14 minutes into climb at 18,000 feet it suffered explosive decompression and disintegrated. An investigation concluded severe corrosion from numerous pressurization cycles caused a pressure-hull rupture. Wreckage was scattered over a 4-mile area in multiple townships.
probable_cause: Severe corrosion of the pressure hull resulted from many pressurization cycles. Cracks produced by corrosion were probably undetected by the inspection program, leading to explosive decompression and structural failure.

factors.evidence: severe corrosion led to a pressure-hull rupture. The severe corrosion was due to the many pressurization flight cycles the aircraft had experienced, and that cracks produced were probably undetected.

The aircraft had previously lost cabin pressure on 5 August; and earlier on the day of the crash, it had departed Songshan Airport, but the crew aborted the flight 10 minutes later for the same reason.

events.text: The aircraft had previously lost cabin pressure on 5 August; and earlier on the day of the crash, it had departed Songshan Airport, but the crew aborted the flight 10 minutes later for the same reason.
After repairs were made, the aircraft departed Songshan Airport again bound for Kaohsiung International Airport.
14 minutes after takeoff, the aircraft suffered an explosive decompression and disintegrated.
The wreckage was scattered across an area 4 mi long, located some 94 mi south of Taipei.
The nose section landed in Sanyi Township, Miaoli County, and other debris landed in the townships of Yuanli, Tongluo, and Tongxiao.

title: Inex-Adria Aviopromet 1308
summary: Inex-Adria Flight 1308, an MD-82 charter flight with 180 Yugoslavian tourists and crew, crashed into Mont San Petru on 1 December 1981 on its final approach to Ajaccio. The crew, unfamiliar with Ajaccio airport, were in a holding pattern over mountainous terrain while ATC mistakenly believed they were over the sea. Imprecise language between crew and controller, combined with the controller's confusion about the aircraft position, led to a fatal clearance to descend into terrain.
probable_cause: The accident resulted from imprecise language used by the crew and air traffic controller. ATC mistakenly believed that Flight 1308 was out of its holding pattern and located over the sea, when in reality the aircraft was located 15 km inland over the mountainous terrain of Corsica. The crew, unfamiliar with the airport and its vicinity, descended on ATC clearance into terrain. The Ajaccio airport lacked radar to detect the conflict.

factors.evidence: imprecise language used by the crew of the MD-82 and the air traffic controller played a significant role

events.text: At 07:28, the plane entered the zone of the control center in Rome, and the flight was cleared to descend to flight level FL 270.
At 07:35, the aircraft entered the air traffic control space in Marseille and the flight crew requested permission for a further reduction in altitude.

ATC control mistakenly believed that Flight 1308 was out of its holding pattern, believing it was already located over the sea, while in reality it was located 15 km inland, over the mountainous terrain of Corsica.
The crew, apparently surprised at the instruction to descend, repeated several times that they were still in the holding pattern.
The aircraft crashed into Mont San Petru on its final approach, killing all 180 passengers and crew on board.
